inserted_link_lines.line: - [connection-proves-access](connection-proves-access.md) asks which shelves a working key leaves unseen, the same boundary that lets a hidden Git name move behind an unchanged advertised list.
- [event-data-honesty](event-data-honesty.md) keeps a vanished listing separate from a cancelled event, just as a vanished advertised name need not mean its stored reference was deleted.
- [[visibility-filter]] names the curtain between stored names and their advertised view, not a lock that keeps the underlying objects private.
- [what-the-gaps-can-say](what-the-gaps-can-say.md) gives this room's partial view a concrete Git example: the shown list can stay still while an unseen stored name moves.
- [[visibility-filter]] names a rule that chooses what reaches the reader, so a working connection cannot by itself certify a complete view.

- [what-the-gaps-can-say](what-the-gaps-can-say.md) shows a Git list changing when only its visibility rule changes, a concrete reminder that leaving a view is not the same as leaving the world it describes.

- [liveness-and-readiness](liveness-and-readiness.md) separates a pulse from an ability to serve, the distinction this ruler needs when a quick error arrives without showing that the requested work recovered.
- [measuring-the-window](measuring-the-window.md) shows why a fast error is no recovery mark: the time taken to answer and the ability to fulfil the request need separate verdicts.

- [closing-the-loop](closing-the-loop.md) offers a human parallel to testing the checker: a reassuring yes can hide a missed check, so a signature test must also show that a known bad mark is refused.

- [checking-a-signed-reply](checking-a-signed-reply.md) gives the reassuring yes a software counterpart: valid examples cannot expose a verifier that accepts every mark, so refusal needs a test of its own.
